limits:
D3DX8 7757e0 (D3DXMatrixInverse, the SSE cofactor inverse) against its original instructions.

The call goes through the thunk 770d10 (JMP [389b7c0]) with dispatch slot 18 (389b7c0) written as
77350c leaves it on an SSE CPU without 3DNow!: both SSE tables (7735f0, 773700) put 7757e0 there.
77350c itself is not executed. Arguments: out, pDeterminant (NULL or not), pM; RET 0xc. The source
matrix sits at a 16-byte aligned or misaligned (+8) address (7757e0 loads it with movlps/movhps only,
so alignment must not matter). Compared: the return (out or NULL), the 16 stored floats, the stored
determinant, untouched sentinels on the NULL path, and MXCSR without its six exception flags.

RCPSS is Unicorn's (QEMU's IEEE single division), not a real CPU's estimate; the native probe uses the
same division model (sse_reciprocal_by_division), so this proves the transcription, not the estimate.
MXCSR control profiles vary the rounding mode only: Unicorn 2.1.4 ignores FZ and DAZ (see the sse_math
report), so they are not exercised here. Cases keep at most one NaN source: Unicorn applies QEMU's x87
NaN rule to SSE operands where hardware returns the first operand's NaN.
flag_mismatches: MXCSR exception flags; Unicorn 2.1.4 raises no SSE exception flags, the native SoftFloat SSE model does. Hardware flags need the Intel capture (roadmap M4)

D3DX8 7716df (D3DXMatrixPerspectiveFovLH as linked into sonic.exe, stdcall, x87 throughout)
against its original instructions.

7716df is called directly (it is not dispatched through the 389b778 table): out, fovy, aspect, near,
far on the stack, RET 0x14. Every case runs the whole body. Compared: the 16 stored floats and the
x87 control word; the six x87 exception flags are compared separately (flag class).

Two profiles:
  primary  Unicorn executes every instruction, including FSINCOS at 0x771706, which QEMU computes
           with the host's double sin/cos (53-bit), not an x87 64-bit-significand reduction. The
           native side uses the Bochs P5/P6 FSINCOS model (third_party/bochs_fpatan, fsincos.cc).
  seeded   the same, but right after 0x771706 ST(0)/ST(1) are overwritten with the native Bochs
           cosine/sine (exported by the probe), so the rest of the body is compared exactly with no
           FSINCOS model difference. Seeding validates the suffix only; it proves nothing about
           Intel FSINCOS.
|fovy * 0.5| >= 2^63 makes FSINCOS set C2 and leave ST(0); the native port returns an explicit unknown
(nullopt) for it, and those cases are counted as native_unknown_cases, not compared.

primary value mismatches are FSINCOS model differences, classified in profiles.primary.mismatch_classes: unicorn_fsincos_infinity_as_out_of_range = QEMU treats FSINCOS(+-inf) as |x| >= 2^63 (C2, ST(0) kept) where the SDM gives #IA with the indefinite NaN (the Bochs model); finite operands use host double sin/cos in Unicorn. The Bochs model is not changed to match Unicorn; settling FSINCOS needs the Intel capture (roadmap M4). This report stays fail while primary mismatches exist
flag_mismatches: x87 exception flags; Unicorn 2.1.4 does not raise PE/UE for most x87 arithmetic, the native SoftFloat/Bochs models do
native_unknown_cases are |fovy/2| >= 2^63 (FSINCOS C2 path); the native port reports them as unknown instead of modelling the stack-underflow stores

d3dx_project.limits:
D3DX8 772615 (Vec3Project) against its original instructions, with the
SSE-path 774310 (MatrixMultiply) and 774150 (Vec3TransformCoord).

The dispatch slots are written as 77350c leaves them on an SSE CPU without
3DNow! (389b784 = 774310, 389b7a0 = 774150); 77350c is not executed. Each case
calls 772615 (stdcall) with any of the projection, view, world and viewport
pointers NULL, and the matrices at 16-byte aligned or misaligned (+8)
addresses, which selects 774150's movaps or movlps path. RCPPS is Unicorn's
(QEMU's float division), not a real CPU's estimate; the native probe uses the
same division model. Cases keep at most one NaN source: Unicorn applies QEMU's
x87 NaN rule (larger significand) to SSE operands, where hardware SSE returns
the first operand's NaN. MXCSR is compared without its six exception flags,
which Unicorn 2.1.4 does not raise. Compared: the three output floats.
The case words (the probe's 61-word input) go to d3dx_project.cases.bin for the
guest override-equivalence test.

ninja_projected_depth.limits:
Projected depth 78dbe0 (stdcall, float w) against original instructions.

78dbe0 compares w with 7e9b40 (FCOMP; below it, or unordered, z = 65535.0, else
z = 1.0f / w through FDIV and FSTP m32), then D3DXVec3Project((0, 0, z),
viewport 3d12780, projection 3d129c0, view = world = 389d318) through thunk
770295 and returns FLD out.z in ST(0) (ret 4). The original runs 770295, 772615,
774310 and 774150 as real code with dispatch slots 3/10/14 written as 77350c
leaves them on an SSE CPU without 3DNow! (774310, 774150, 772615); 77350c is not
executed. Cases: w at the 7e9b40 edge and its neighbours, signed zeros,
negatives, infinities, denormals, NaNs, and typical depths; integer viewports
including zero/negative extents; perspective-like and random projections; the
image's 389d318 or random words; four masked x87 control words and the MXCSR
rounding modes. Compared: the returned ext80 (bitwise), that exactly one value
was pushed (TOP and tag), EAX (772615's pOut, entry ESP - 0xc). RCPPS is
Unicorn's QEMU division, the same model the native port uses; cases keep at
most one NaN source (Unicorn applies the x87 NaN rule to SSE operands). x87
exception flags are compared separately: Unicorn 2.1.4 raises no PE for an
inexact FDIV/FSTP (1/w for most w) nor IE/DE for NaN/denormal operands, which
the native model raises as the SDM documents, so nearly every case differs in
flags only (verdict partial); MXCSR flags are not compared. ECX/EDX (772615's
leftovers) and the x87 condition bits C0/C2/C3 (undefined after the trailing
FLD/FDIV) are not compared. The case words go to ninja_projected_depth.cases.bin.

ninja_queue_color.limits:
Render-queue colour 402f40 (with its 77ff90 tail jump) against original instructions.

402f40 (cdecl, pointer to four floats) copies the colour into 3ab9864 word by
word, clamps each component to [-1, 1] with FLD/FCOMP against 7dcb10 (1.0) and
7dcb0c (-1.0), then jumps to 77ff90(&3ab9864), which copies the four words into
3d0f7f0. Cases: finite values around the clamp edges, signed zeros, infinities,
denormals, quiet and signalling NaNs (any number per case: nothing is computed,
so no NaN-propagation rule applies), under the four masked x87 control words
the game uses. Compared: the eight stored words (bitwise), and EAX/ECX/EDX and
the x87 condition bits after the call against the values the source leaves
(EAX = 3ab9864, ECX/EDX = the last two copied words, C3/C2/C0 = the last FCOMP).
x87 exception flags are compared separately: Unicorn 2.1.4 raises neither IE
for a NaN FCOMP operand / SNaN FLD nor DE for a denormal FLD m32, which the
native model raises as the Intel SDM documents, so those cases differ in flags
only (verdict partial). Unmasked-exception control words are not exercised.
The corpus (CW, the input words, the prior 3ab9864 words) goes to
ninja_queue_color.cases.bin for the guest override-equivalence test.

limits:
781570 / 781250 / 791170 (the camera block, view matrix and projection WinMain sets at 402d4f..402d5e)
against their original instructions.

Every instruction of 781570, 781250 and 791170 runs, with all their callees from the original bytes:
788290/7883c0 (the 88af78 sine table), 7871f0, 787e30, 7716df, 770804 -> 774310 and 770d10 -> 7757e0
(dispatch slots 389b784 / 389b7c0 written as 77350c leaves them on an SSE CPU without 3DNow!; 77350c is
not executed). The D3D8 device is a fixture: [3d128b0] -> object -> vtable whose +0x94 (SetTransform)
and +0x9c (MultiplyTransform) are `ret 0xc` stubs that record (state, the 16 words passed). The matrix
stack is a fixture block of 1..4 slots at [3d0fa1c] with a random current depth. Mode 0 runs 781570
(thiscall, ECX = 3aad0a0) and then 781250; mode 1 runs 781250 on a random block.

Compared: 3d0f760 (view), matrix-stack slot 0, 3d0f818 (current = base) and 3d0fa2c (depth),
3d0f980, 3d0f9e0, 3d0f808, 3d0f968, 3d12960, 3d129c0, 389d398, 389d358 (sentinel when 7757e0
returns NULL), the block after 781570, the three device calls and the x87 control word.

Two profiles:
  primary  Unicorn executes FPTAN (791240), FPATAN (79124a) and FSINCOS (771706) itself: QEMU computes
           them with host doubles, the native side with the Bochs P5/P6 models.
  seeded   right after each of those instructions the result registers are overwritten with the native
           Bochs results (exported by the probe), so every other instruction is compared exactly.
           Seeding proves the transcription, not Intel FPTAN/FPATAN/FSINCOS (roadmap M4).
RCPSS/RCPPS are Unicorn's IEEE division in both the source and the native probe (not a real CPU's
estimate). MXCSR profiles vary the rounding mode only (Unicorn ignores FZ/DAZ). At most one NaN source per
case (Unicorn applies the x87 NaN rule to SSE operands). VIEW_SMOKE=1 in the environment stops each profile
after 300 cases (for mutant runs); the recorded report never uses it.

primary value mismatches come from FPTAN/FPATAN/FSINCOS: Unicorn uses host doubles, the native Bochs models are not changed to match; settling them needs the Intel capture (roadmap M4). The report stays fail while they exist; the seeded profile is the transcription check
x87 and MXCSR exception flags are not compared (Unicorn 2.1.4 raises few x87 and no SSE flags)
